case_number: WP No. 10114 of 2026 and WMP. No. 10918 of 2026

judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

M. Dhandapani, J.:— This petition has been filed seeking to quash the impugned online order dated Nil passed by the 4th Respondent in Application No. TN 720250930358 and consequently direct the 4th respondent to issue Legal heirship certificate for the petitioner considering his online application dated 30-9-2025.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that he got legally married with one Suseela. Out of the wedlock, the petitioner blessed with one son and two daughters. The petitioner's son Dineshkumar married to one Priyanka. Out of the said wedlock, they have blessed with two sons. Suddenly, the petitioners son died in an accident on 4-9-2025 leaving behind his parents, wife and sons. After death of his son, the petitioner made an online application for issuance of legal heirship certificate on 30-9-2025 along with necessary documents. However, the said application has been rejected by the 4th respondent on the ground that the deceased was living in Karur and his family card does not have the names of his wife and children. Challenging the same, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner's son and her daughter in law are the bank employees and they were living in Karur. The petitioner has produced documents to prove the relationship of the deceased with all the five legal heirs and if the 4th respondent had doubt over the same, he would have conduct enquiry by summoning the petitioner and other legal heirs but mere rejection cannot be sustained and the said impugned order is liable to be set aside. Therefore, this Court may remand the matter back to the authorities and pass appropriate orders.

4. The learned government advocate appearing for the respondents have not raised any objection.

5. Heard the learned counsel for both side and perused the materials available on record.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the fair submission made by the parties, this court sets aside the impugned order dated nil passed by the 4th respondent and remands the matter back to the 4th respondent for fresh consideration. After conducting enquiry, the 4th respondent is directed to issue legal heirship certificate of the deceased A. Dinesh Kumar to the eligible persons within a period of three weeks from today and file a report before this Court on or before 6-4-2026.

7. With the above observation and directions, the writ petition is allowed. No costs. Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.

8. Post the matter on 6-4-2026 “for reporting compliance”.
